P1.evidence: Rep referenced the application ('I read your application, so I have a bit of a head start') but did not read setter notes back. Frame was three-part not four — 'where you're at in your fitness journey, what you're looking to accomplish, what's missing' with no 'what you need'. Frame agreement asked ('That sound good?'). Open question asked ('what could we potentially help you with').

P2.evidence: No baseline was taken. Age (63), the torn meniscus, current training and diet were all volunteered unprompted inside the prospect's first answer; the script credits asking, so every check is a miss rather than a hit. The call dropped before the rep could return to them.

P5.evidence: Call ended before consequence framing was possible.

P6.evidence: Call ended before any commitment check.

notes: Opening frame was clean but three-part. The recoverable failure here is infrastructure, not skill: two connectivity drops in eight minutes killed a booked call with a 63-year-old who arrived already sold on kettlebells. Whoever re-runs it must take a real P2 baseline — the meniscus tear was volunteered and never followed up.
